automation_name: AI Security Wiki Topic News Collector

cutoff_window.rule: Include only public items visibly published or updated within the last 2 days relative to run time; exclude missing, ambiguous, future-dated, or boundary-only dates.

searched_topics: agent and tool security including MCP, plugins, browsers, delegated authority, and autonomous action
identity, authentication, authorization, credentials, and least privilege
model, dataset, dependency, artifact, runtime, cloud, hardware, and deployment supply chains
threat modeling, red teaming, security evaluation, assurance, monitoring, and release gates
AI security standards, regulation, governance, audit evidence, and risk management
public AI security incidents, mitigations, patches, disclosures, and lessons learned

federation_context.local_scope: AI-specific security facts, controls, incidents, vulnerabilities, assurance, governance, and operational implications.
federation_context.upstream_scope: Broad AI entities belong in ai-wiki; general AI-assisted development practices belong in ai-dev-wiki.

qualifying_findings.title: Kimi Code FetchURL SSRF hardening bypass disclosed as CVE-2026-17534
qualifying_findings.summary: NVD published CVE-2026-17534 for MoonshotAI Kimi Code before 0.27.0. The FetchURL tool relied on a static hostname and IP-literal denylist without DNS resolution or redirect re-validation, so prompt-influenced FetchURL calls could reach loopback or internal services. FetchURL was included in the default auto-approve tool set, so manual mode did not require interactive user confirmation.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: MoonshotAI Kimi Code @moonshot-ai/kimi-code versions before 0.27.0; affected files include local-fetch-url providers and default tool approval policy.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: This is a concrete agent-tool boundary failure: prompt injection can steer an auto-approved network fetch tool across an intended internal-network isolation boundary.

upstream_routing.local_security_note: Keep the SSRF, auto-approval, prompt-influenced tool-call, and patch boundary in ai-security-wiki.
upstream_routing.ai_wiki: Kimi Code and MoonshotAI are broad AI/developer-tool entities if durable entity coverage is needed.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General coding-agent tool approval practice and developer workflow implications belong upstream in ai-dev-wiki.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence: NVD record has an in-window publication date, CVE details, affected version range, CWE, CVSS vector from CNA, and vendor patch references.
follow_up_actions: Track whether Kimi Code 0.27.0 or later appears in local dependency inventories before any ingest.
When ingesting, connect this finding to local agent-tool approval, SSRF, and internal-service isolation pages rather than creating a duplicate broad Kimi Code page.

qualifying_findings.title: NVIDIA and partners launch Open Secure AI Alliance for AI safety and security tooling
qualifying_findings.summary: NVIDIA announced the Open Secure AI Alliance as an industry coalition to build and share open technologies, techniques, and tools for AI safety and cybersecurity. NVIDIA framed the coalition around open models, harnesses, guardrails, identity, permissions, logs, evaluation, and agent-stack controls, citing the Hugging Face incident as evidence that defenders need inspectable and locally runnable AI defensive systems.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: AI defensive tooling ecosystem; agent harnesses, open-weight defensive models, identity controls, safe model formats, supply-chain patches, multi-model scanning, and secure coding workflows.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: This is a governance and assurance change: major AI and security vendors are organizing open defensive infrastructure for AI agent stacks, including auditable harnesses and identity controls.

upstream_routing.local_security_note: Keep security-specific implications for open defensive models, auditable agent harnesses, identity, and incident-response constraints in ai-security-wiki.
upstream_routing.ai_wiki: The coalition, NVIDIA, HPE, CrowdStrike, Hugging Face, Microsoft, Safetensors, and broad model/tool catalog details are upstream-owned AI ecosystem entities.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General open-source development and secure coding workflow practices belong in ai-dev-wiki when not security-specific.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence: multiple official in-window posts describe the same coalition and security mission.
follow_up_actions: Monitor whether the alliance publishes concrete tools, specs, repositories, or evaluation artifacts that should become durable local security pages.
During ingest, avoid duplicating broad company or product descriptions already owned by ai-wiki.

qualifying_findings.title: Microsoft introduces Project Perception and MAI-Cyber-1-Flash for agentic security workflows
qualifying_findings.summary: Microsoft announced Project Perception as an agentic security system using red-team, blue-team, and green-team agents over a new Cyber Stack. The first scenario brings MAI-Cyber-1-Flash into MDASH, a software vulnerability multi-model agent team; Microsoft says this configuration reaches 96% on CyberGym and nearly 50% cost savings versus the current MDASH configuration.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Microsoft Project Perception public preview planned for 2026-08-03; MAI-Cyber-1-Flash inside MDASH for software vulnerability management.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: This is a concrete change in AI-assisted assurance: a major security vendor is packaging specialized cyber models and coordinated agents for vulnerability discovery, triage, and remediation workflows.

upstream_routing.local_security_note: Keep the security-agent architecture, vulnerability-management assurance claim, human-control boundary, and benchmark claim in ai-security-wiki.
upstream_routing.ai_wiki: Microsoft AI, MAI model-family background, and broad product/entity coverage are upstream-owned.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General AI-assisted development workflow or secure SDLC usage patterns belong in ai-dev-wiki unless tied to security assurance controls.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence for announcement facts and dates; benchmark and cost claims are vendor-stated and should be treated as claims until independently evaluated.
follow_up_actions: Check for the public preview or technical documentation after 2026-08-03.
If ingested, record benchmark and cost figures as Microsoft-stated claims, not independent assurance results.

qualifying_findings.title: European Commission publishes Cyber Resilience Act implementation guidance

related_deadlines: 2027-12-11 main Cyber Resilience Act obligations apply

qualifying_findings.summary: The European Commission published practical guidance for implementing the Cyber Resilience Act. The guidance clarifies product scope, substantial modification, support periods, reporting obligations, and risk assessment requirements. The Commission explicitly tied swift CRA implementation to recent frontier AI models with cybersecurity capabilities.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Digital products placed on the EU market; CRA reporting obligations from 2026-09-11 and main obligations from 2027-12-11.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: AI systems with software, model, tool, runtime, or device surfaces may need lifecycle cybersecurity evidence, vulnerability handling, and reporting readiness under CRA-aligned governance.

upstream_routing.local_security_note: Keep CRA risk assessment, vulnerability handling, reporting, lifecycle evidence, and frontier-AI cyber-capability implications in ai-security-wiki.
upstream_routing.ai_wiki: Broad EU policy and AI Act background belong upstream when not security-specific.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General software-development implementation practices belong in ai-dev-wiki unless they define security evidence or release gates.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence: official Commission pages show in-window publication and last-update dates; legal applicability details should be verified against the downloaded guidance during ingest.
follow_up_actions: Download and review the CRA guidance annex before durable synthesis.
Map relevant obligations to AI security release gates, audit evidence, vulnerability handling, and product lifecycle pages.
